title: Active learning identifies a protoglobin variant with 99% yield and cis-selective cyclopropanation
summary: An iterative machine-learning campaign engineered the protoglobin from Pyrobaculum arsenaticum (ParPgb) for non-native cyclopropanation of 4-vinylanisole. After two model-guided rounds following an initial library screen, variant MPFDY gave 99% total cyclopropane yield and a 14:1 cis:trans ratio in the reported assay, compared with a parent variant that produced about 40% yield and favored trans product. The result demonstrates a specific sequence combination with improved yield and stereoselectivity in this enzyme scaffold.
ai_technology: ALDE (Active Learning-assisted Directed Evolution), using a bootstrapped deep-neural-network ensemble and Thompson sampling
organization: California Institute of Technology; University of California, Berkeley; Elegen Corp

evidence.tested: After two model-guided rounds following an initial library screen, variant MPFDY gave 99% total cyclopropane yield and a 14:1 cis:trans ratio in the reported assay, compared with a parent variant that produced about 40% yield and favored trans product.
evidence.unknown: Cyclopropanation is an established non-native enzyme reaction class; the study's distinct result is the ALDE-guided ParPgb sequence and its measured product yield/selectivity. The 99% yield and 14:1 ratio are study assay results, not evidence of industrial process readiness. The study is a single enzyme-engineering campaign.
evidence.ai_role: ALDE trained on measured sequence–yield data, quantified model uncertainty, and selected variants across two iterative rounds in a five-residue, 3.2-million-sequence design space. Experimental screening measured product yield and stereoselectivity; the model-guided variants included MPFDY, whose combined mutations improved the targeted cis-product objective where tested single mutations and their naive recombinations did not.
